hovers.markdown:
**G92** — Threading pass as a cycle

Cuts one threading pass, straight or tapered, and returns to the start point, so a thread is written as a list of X values\. F is the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate\. On a mill and in G\-code system B the same number sets the coordinate system and clamps the spindle speed instead\. A threading pass carries no S word, so gEdit reads the S of a G92 block as that speed clamp rather than as a speed to scale — which is what protects a system\-B program opened with a system\-A machine\.

The feed carries the thread pitch here, so changing it changes the thread\.
